claims: The baker's math for sourdough is: Flour - 100%; Water - 67%; Starter - 20-25 %; and Salt - 2%.
This means whatever amount of flour you use to make your sourdough, water should be 67% of its weight, the starter 20 to 25%, and the salt 2% of the flour.

Our tool is partially based on baker's math, as we allow the user to enter the amount of water freely and not limit it to 67%, because everyone has their own preference when it comes to the hydration of the sourdough.
To evaluate the amount of the starter, you may use the following formula: starter = 20% × amount of flour The starter is 20% of the amount of flour you're using to make your sourdough.
Still, if you want to follow the proper proportions to make your sourdough, the ratio of salt is supposed to be 2% of the amount of flour you are using.
The starter is 20% of the amount of flour that you're using to make your sourdough.
If you are using baker's percentage to calculate the ratio of ingredients of your sourdough, then the hydration of your dough is 67%.
It means you should add 536 ml of water to make your sourdough.

The amount of starter needed in sourdough is 20% of the flour, but it also depends on the temperature - higher temperatures require a lesser amount, and lower temperatures require a higher amount of starter.
You need 120 grams of starter to add to 600 grams of flour for sourdough.
